Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ with $n \ge 1$, let $\mathbb{R}^n$ be the set of functions
$n \to \mathbb{R}$ ([[lem-metrics-on-rn]]) carrying the product topology of $n$
copies of the usual topology of $\mathbb{R}$ ([[def-product-topology]]), and let
$d_2$ be the Euclidean metric. Then:

1. The product topology on $\mathbb{R}^n$ **is** the metric topology of $d_2$
   ([[def-metric-topology]]), so $\mathbb{R}^n$ as a product and $\mathbb{R}^n$ as
   a metric space are one topological space, and it is metrizable
   ([[def-metrizable-space]]).
2. A subset $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is a compact subset for the product
   topology ([[def-compact-space]]) **if and only if** $K$ is closed in
   $\mathbb{R}^n$ and bounded ([[def-metric-bounded-diameter]]).

The hypothesis $n \ge 1$ is inherited from [[lem-metrics-on-rn]], which defines
$\mathbb{R}^n$ and its three metrics only there; for $n = 0$ the product is a
one-point space and is compact. **No choice principle is used**: the metric
statement it is read off from is proved by bisection
([[thm-heine-borel-rn]]).

derivations.claim: If $P^*=P$ and $P^2=P$, then $\mathbb C^N=\operatorname{ran}P\oplus\ker P$: every $x$ equals $Px+(x-Px)$, and the intersection is zero. The two summands are orthogonal because $\langle Pu,y\rangle=\langle u,P^*y\rangle=0$ for $y\in\ker P$. An orthonormal basis adapted to this decomposition makes $P$ diagonal with one $1$ for each basis vector in $\operatorname{ran}P$ and zero otherwise. Trace is invariant under change of basis, so $\operatorname{tr}P=\dim_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{ran}P$, while $\|P\|_F^2=\operatorname{tr}(P^*P)=\operatorname{tr}(P^2)=k$. Thus the stated equations are exactly the orthogonal projections onto $k$-planes, and every such plane has one unique projection.

For fixed $k$, the equations $P^*=P$, $P^2=P$, and $\operatorname{tr}P=k$ are closed conditions on the real and imaginary matrix entries, and step 1.1 bounds the Frobenius norm by $\sqrt{k}$. Since $2N^2\ge1$, [F1] makes $\operatorname{Gr}_{\mathbb C}(k,N)$ compact. There are finitely many indices $k$; restricting any open cover of their union to each compact member gives a finite subcover for that member, and the union of these finitely many finite subfamilies is finite. Hence $\mathscr G_N$ is compact.

citations.quote: Let $N\ge2$. For $1\le k<N$, let $\operatorname{Gr}_{\mathbb C}(k,N)$ be the set of matrices $P\in M_N(\mathbb C)$ satisfying $P^*=P$, $P^2=P$, and $\operatorname{tr}P=k$, with the topology inherited from $M_N(\mathbb C)\cong\mathbb R^{2N^2}$. The map $P\mapsto\operatorname{ran}P$ identifies this space with the usual Grassmannian of complex $k$-planes in $\mathbb C^N$. The finite union $\mathscr G_N=\bigcup_{1\le k<N}\operatorname{Gr}_{\mathbb C}(k,N)$ is compact.

Let $F:M^m\to N^n$ be smooth, let $q\in N$ be a regular value, and assume
$F^{-1}(q)$ is nonempty. Then $F^{-1}(q)$ is an embedded submanifold of
codimension $n$. Equivalently, it has dimension $m-n$.

derivations.claim:
Regard $M_m(\mathbb C)$ as $\mathbb R^{2m^2}$ and the Hermitian matrices as a real vector space of dimension $m^2$. On the open set of invertible matrices, the smooth map $\Theta(Q)=Q^*Q$ has derivative $d\Theta_Q(X)=Q^*X+X^*Q$. At a unitary $Q$, every Hermitian $H$ is the derivative value for $X=\tfrac12 QH$. Thus $I_m$ is a regular value and [F2] makes $U(m)=\Theta^{-1}(I_m)$ a manifold of dimension $m^2$. The determinant map $U(m)\to S^1$ is a submersion: at the identity its derivative on a skew-Hermitian tangent matrix $X$ is $\operatorname{tr}X$, which reaches the tangent line $i\mathbb R$ by $X=itI_m/m$, and translation gives surjectivity at every group element. Consequently $SU(m)=\det^{-1}(1)$ has dimension $m^2-1$. The same determinant argument for $(U(k)\times U(N-k))\to S^1$, $(U,V)\mapsto\det U\det V$, shows that
$$H_k=\{\operatorname{diag}(U,V):U\in U(k),\,V\in U(N-k),\,\det U\det V=1\}$$
is a closed Lie subgroup of dimension $k^2+(N-k)^2-1$.

Fix a $k$-plane $V_0$ and its orthogonal complement. A plane transverse to $V_0^\perp$ is the graph of a unique complex-linear map $T:V_0\to V_0^\perp$. The graph projection is
$$
P_T=\begin{pmatrix}I\\T\end{pmatrix}(I+T^*T)^{-1}\begin{pmatrix}I&T^*\end{pmatrix},
$$
and its inverse chart is $T=(P_T)_{21}(P_T)_{11}^{-1}$. These formulas are smooth, and such planes form an open neighborhood because invertibility of $(P)_{11}$ is an open matrix condition. Thus the Grassmannian has local charts modeled on $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(V_0,V_0^\perp)$ and real dimension $2k(N-k)$.

On a sufficiently small graph chart, Gram–Schmidt applied to the columns of $\binom I T$ and $\binom{-T^*}I$ gives a smoothly varying unitary matrix $Q(T)$ carrying $V_0$ to the graph of $T$; all normalization denominators are positive because each list is linearly independent. A unitary matrix preserving a plane also preserves its orthogonal complement. Therefore $g_iV_P=V_P$ exactly when $Q(T)^*g_iQ(T)$ is block diagonal and belongs to $H_k$. The map $$(T,h_1,\ldots,h_r)\longmapsto(Q(T)h_1Q(T)^*,\ldots,Q(T)h_rQ(T)^*,P_T)$$ and its inverse are smooth local coordinates for $I_{k,r}$. Hence $I_{k,r}$ is an embedded submanifold with dimension $2k(N-k)+r\dim H_k$. It is closed because it is the zero set of the continuous matrix equations $g_iP-Pg_i=0$.

Substituting $\dim H_k=k^2+(N-k)^2-1$ gives the displayed dimension. Since $\dim SU(N)=N^2-1$, subtraction from the ambient product dimension gives codimension $r\bigl((N^2-1)-(k^2+(N-k)^2-1)\bigr)=2r\,k(N-k)$. Subtracting $\dim I_{k,r}$ from $\dim SU(N)^r=r(N^2-1)$ instead gives $2(r-1)k(N-k)$, the dimension deficit used when the plane variable is included in the source of a holonomy family.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Let $\mathcal A_\infty:=A_0+\Omega^1(M,\operatorname{ad}P)$ and let $\mathcal G_\infty$ be the smooth gauge group, with the $C^\infty$ section topology generated by all finite-atlas derivative seminorms. Define $\bar{\mathcal G}_\infty:=\mathcal G_\infty/Z_N$. In a local section of $P$, write a connection as a matrix-valued one-form $A$ and a gauge section as a map $u$ into $SU(N)$; the right gauge action is $A^u:=u^{-1}Au+u^{-1}du$, equivalently pullback by the gauge automorphism associated with $u$. The calculus lemma proves that this formula defines a smooth action on the Sobolev spaces above. For an adjoint section $\xi$, set $d_A\xi:=d\xi+[A,\xi]$ using the degree-one Lie-algebra-valued-form bracket. In local coordinates and an orthonormal adjoint frame, define the formal adjoint on an adjoint-valued one-form $a$ by $(d_A^*a)=-g^{ij}(\nabla_i^{\mathrm{LC}}a_j+[A_i,a_j])$, where $\nabla^{\mathrm{LC}}$ differentiates the covector index. This is the $L^2$ adjoint for the Riemannian volume and stated fiber metric; its local coefficient formula defines a distribution at Sobolev regularity.

Assume the configuration data and integer $k>d/2+1$ from the preceding definition, and let $\mathcal A_k^*$ be the locus where the holonomy representation on $\mathbb C^N$ is irreducible. For any $A\in\mathcal A_k$, evaluation at $p_m$ identifies its stabilizer in $\mathcal G_{k+1}$ with the centralizer of $\operatorname{Hol}_{p_m}(A)$ in $SU(N)$. Thus an irreducible connection has stabilizer exactly $Z_N$, and the induced action of $\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1}=\mathcal G_{k+1}/Z_N$ on $\mathcal A_k^*$ is free. The subset $\mathcal A_k^*$ is open in $\mathcal A_k$.

The Sobolev action is proper: if $A_j\to A$ and $A_j^{u_j}\to B$ in $H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ for sequences $A_j,A,B\in\mathcal A_k$ and $u_j\in\mathcal G_{k+1}$, then some subsequence $u_{j_\ell}$ converges in $H^{k+1}(\operatorname{Ad}P)$ to $u\in\mathcal G_{k+1}$ and $B=A^u$. Equivalently, the action map $\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1}\times\mathcal A_k^*\to\mathcal A_k^*\times\mathcal A_k^*$ is proper, meaning inverse images of compact sets are compact.

Let $N\ge2$. For $1\le k<N$, let $\operatorname{Gr}_{\mathbb C}(k,N)$ be the set of matrices $P\in M_N(\mathbb C)$ satisfying $P^*=P$, $P^2=P$, and $\operatorname{tr}P=k$, with the topology inherited from $M_N(\mathbb C)\cong\mathbb R^{2N^2}$. The map $P\mapsto\operatorname{ran}P$ identifies this space with the usual Grassmannian of complex $k$-planes in $\mathbb C^N$. The finite union $\mathscr G_N=\bigcup_{1\le k<N}\operatorname{Gr}_{\mathbb C}(k,N)$ is compact.

1. **Continuous images.** If $f : X \to Y$ is continuous
   ([[def-continuous-map-top]]) and $(X, \mathcal{T}_X)$ is compact
   ([[def-compact-space]]), then $f[X]$ is a compact subset of $Y$. More
   generally, if $K \subseteq X$ is a compact subset of $X$ then $f[K]$ is a
   compact subset of $Y$.
2. **Extreme values.** If $(X, \mathcal{T}_X)$ is compact and nonempty and
   $g : X \to \mathbb{R}$ is continuous, then $g[X]$ has a maximum and a minimum
   ([[def-max-min]]): there are $x_{\max}, x_{\min} \in X$ with
   $$g(x_{\min}) \;\le\; g(x) \;\le\; g(x_{\max}) \qquad \text{for every } x \in X .$$
3. **Compact to Hausdorff.** If $(X, \mathcal{T}_X)$ is compact, $(Y,
   \mathcal{T}_Y)$ is Hausdorff ([[def-hausdorff-space]]) and $f : X \to Y$ is a
   continuous bijection, then $f$ is a homeomorphism
   ([[def-homeomorphism-and-open-maps]]).

Let $I=[a,b]\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty compact interval, let
$C:I\to M_n(\mathbb R)$ be continuous, let $t_0\in I$, and let
$Y_0\in M_n(\mathbb R)$. For $n=0$, there is exactly one map $Y:I\to M_0(\mathbb R)$, namely the empty-matrix map, and all entrywise differential identities are vacuous. For $n\ge1$ and $a<b$, the linear matrix initial value problem

$$Y'(t)=C(t)Y(t),\qquad Y(t_0)=Y_0,$$

has a unique solution on all of $I$, with domain-relative one-sided
derivatives at the endpoints. If $n\ge1$ and $a=b$, then $t_0=a$ and there is exactly
one map $Y:I\to M_n(\mathbb R)$ with $Y(a)=Y_0$. This singleton map
extends to a solution of $Z'=C(a)Z$, $Z(a)=Y_0$, on an open interval
around $a$; any two such local continuations agree on their common interval
containing $a$. No time derivative or IVP solution on the singleton itself
is asserted.

derivations.claim: By [F1], $\mathcal A_\infty^*$ is exactly the set of connections whose holonomy action has no common proper nonzero invariant subspace. By [F2], for each such connection the stabilizer in the stated Sobolev gauge group is $Z_N$. The latter is the conditional stabilizer conclusion recorded separately from the holonomy criterion.

For each $V\in\mathscr G_N$, irreducibility supplies a based piecewise-smooth loop $\ell_V$ whose holonomy $g_V=\operatorname{Hol}_A(\ell_V)$ does not preserve $V$. If $P_V$ is the orthogonal projection onto $V$, then $(I-P_V)g_VP_V\ne0$. For each fixed loop $\ell$, the set of $V$ with $(I-P_V)\operatorname{Hol}_A(\ell)P_V\ne0$ is open, since the projector topology and matrix multiplication are continuous. These open sets cover $\mathscr G_N$.

Compactness in [F3] gives a finite subcover, hence finitely many loops $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_r$ for which no proper nonzero subspace is invariant under every $g_j=\operatorname{Hol}_A(\ell_j)$. The case $r=0$ cannot cover the nonempty space $\mathscr G_N$, so $r\ge1$.

Define the continuous function
$$h_A(P)=\sum_{j=1}^r\|(I-P)g_jP\|_F$$
on $\mathscr G_N$, where $\|\cdot\|_F$ is the Frobenius norm. It is positive at every $P$ by step 2.1. By [F4] it has a minimum $\delta>0$, and $h_A(P)\ge\delta$ for every $P\in\mathscr G_N$.

On a smooth segment of any chosen loop, write parallel transport as $U'=-B(t)U$, where $B(t)\in\mathfrak{su}(N)$ is the connection form contracted with the path tangent; [F5] gives the unique solution on the whole segment. For a nearby connection with coefficient $B+b$, let $\widetilde U$ be its solution and put $W=U^{-1}\widetilde U$. Differentiation gives $W'=-U^{-1}bU\,W$, $W(0)=I$, and skew-Hermiticity makes both $U$ and $W$ unitary. The integral equation therefore gives $\|W(1)-I\|_F\le\int\|b(t)\|_F\,dt$. A $C^1$ perturbation of the connection makes each of the finitely many segment integrals arbitrarily small, so finite composition shows all $g_j$ vary continuously in the stated $C^1$ topology. Choose a neighborhood with $\|g_j(A')-g_j(A)\|_F<\delta/(2r)$ for every $j$.

For any orthogonal projection $P$, both $\|P\|_{\mathrm{op}}$ and $\|I-P\|_{\mathrm{op}}$ are at most $1$. Thus $$\left|\|(I-P)\operatorname{Hol}_{A'}(\ell_j)P\|_F-\|(I-P)g_jP\|_F\right|\le\|\operatorname{Hol}_{A'}(\ell_j)-g_j\|_F.$$ Summing over $j$ and using step 4.1 together with the uniform positive margin from step 3.1 gives $h_{A'}(P)>\delta/2$ uniformly in $P$. Hence the same finite tuple has no common invariant proper nonzero subspace for every such $A'$.

A $C^1$ neighborhood on the compact base is specified by finitely many continuous section seminorms; each is continuous in the $C^\infty$ section topology. Therefore the neighborhood in step 4.1 is also a $C^\infty$ neighborhood, and $\mathcal A_\infty^*$ is open. step 2.1 gives the finite holonomy witness at $A$, and step 1.1 gives the stated stabilizer.

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a compact, connected, oriented, boundaryless smooth manifold of dimension $d\in\{3,4\}$ with a smooth Riemannian metric, let $N\ge2$, and fix a smooth right principal $SU(N)$-bundle $\pi:P\to M$, a smooth connection $A_0$, and a point $p_m\in P$ over $x_m\in M$. Use the standard unitary representation of $SU(N)$ on $\mathbb C^N$ and the invariant positive inner product $\langle X,Y\rangle=-\operatorname{tr}(XY)$ on $\mathfrak{su}(N)$. Define the adjoint vector bundle $\operatorname{ad}P=P\times_{\operatorname{Ad}}\mathfrak{su}(N)$ and the adjoint group bundle $\operatorname{Ad}P=P\times_{\operatorname{Ad}}SU(N)$ with associated-bundle relation $[pg,z]=[p,\operatorname{Ad}_g z]$.

Choose one finite smooth bundle atlas with relatively compact coordinate domains and a subordinate partition of unity. For each integer $k>d/2+1$, let $H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ and $H^{k+1}(\operatorname{ad}P)$ be the Sobolev completions of smooth sections in the resulting finite-atlas norms. Define the affine configuration space $\mathcal A_k:=A_0+H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ and the set $\mathcal G_{k+1}:=H^{k+1}(\operatorname{Ad}P)$ of Sobolev gauge sections. The next lemma proves that the pointwise product and inverse close on this set and make it a Hilbert Lie group. Its based subset is $\mathcal G_{k+1,m}:=\{u\in\mathcal G_{k+1}:u(p_m)=e\}$. Let $Z_N=\{zI_N:z^N=1\}$ be the center of $SU(N)$, viewed as constant gauge sections. Indeed, if $Z=(z_{ij})$ is central and $D=\operatorname{diag}(t_1,\ldots,t_N)\in SU(N)$, then $(t_j-t_i)z_{ij}=0$. For each $i\ne j$ one can choose such a diagonal matrix with $t_i\ne t_j$, so $Z$ is diagonal. Commuting with the determinant-one unitary rotation whose block on the $(i,j)$ coordinates is $\begin{pmatrix}\cos t&\sin t\\-\sin t&\cos t\end{pmatrix}$ for $t\notin\pi\mathbb Z$ forces the $i$th and $j$th diagonal entries equal. Hence $Z=zI_N$; determinant one gives $z^N=1$, and conversely every such scalar is central. Write $\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1}$ for the set of $Z_N$-cosets with quotient topology; the next lemma also verifies that the induced pointwise operation makes it a Hilbert Lie group.

Let $\mathcal A_\infty:=A_0+\Omega^1(M,\operatorname{ad}P)$ and let $\mathcal G_\infty$ be the smooth gauge group, with the $C^\infty$ section topology generated by all finite-atlas derivative seminorms. Define $\bar{\mathcal G}_\infty:=\mathcal G_\infty/Z_N$. In a local section of $P$, write a connection as a matrix-valued one-form $A$ and a gauge section as a map $u$ into $SU(N)$; the right gauge action is $A^u:=u^{-1}Au+u^{-1}du$, equivalently pullback by the gauge automorphism associated with $u$. The calculus lemma proves that this formula defines a smooth action on the Sobolev spaces above. For an adjoint section $\xi$, set $d_A\xi:=d\xi+[A,\xi]$ using the degree-one Lie-algebra-valued-form bracket. In local coordinates and an orthonormal adjoint frame, define the formal adjoint on an adjoint-valued one-form $a$ by $(d_A^*a)=-g^{ij}(\nabla_i^{\mathrm{LC}}a_j+[A_i,a_j])$, where $\nabla^{\mathrm{LC}}$ differentiates the covector index. This is the $L^2$ adjoint for the Riemannian volume and stated fiber metric; its local coefficient formula defines a distribution at Sobolev regularity.

For $A\in\mathcal A_k$, parallel transport of its $C^1$ connection form around piecewise smooth loops based at $p_m$ defines a subgroup $\operatorname{Hol}_{p_m}(A)\subseteq SU(N)$. Call $A$ irreducible when this subgroup leaves no nonzero proper complex subspace of $\mathbb C^N$ invariant; changing the chosen frame conjugates the subgroup and leaves this condition unchanged. Write $\mathcal A_k^*$ and $\mathcal A_\infty^*$ for the irreducible loci. Once the calculus lemma verifies the group action, define orbit equivalence by $A\sim B$ exactly when $B=A^u$ for some gauge section $u$; all resulting quotients carry the quotient topology, whose open sets are those with open inverse image under the orbit projection.

Assume ZF together with the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be $S^3$ or $S^4$ with its compact, connected, oriented, boundaryless smooth structure and a smooth Riemannian metric. Let $N\ge2$, let $P\to M$ be a smooth principal right $SU(N)$-bundle, choose a smooth reference connection $A_0$, a basepoint $m\in M$, and a frame of the fiber $P_m$. Put $\mathcal A_\infty=A_0+\Omega^1(M;\operatorname{ad}P)$ with its $C^\infty$ section topology. For a smooth connection $A$, let $\operatorname{Hol}_A\subseteq SU(N)$ be the group generated by parallel transports along based piecewise-smooth loops at $m$, expressed in the chosen frame. Call $A$ irreducible when the standard action of $\operatorname{Hol}_A$ on $\mathbb C^N$ has no nonzero proper invariant complex subspace, and write $\mathcal A_\infty^*$ for this locus. For each integer $q>\dim(M)/2+1$, let $\mathcal G_{q+1}$ be the $H^{q+1}$ gauge group of sections of $\operatorname{Ad}P$, acting on $H^q$ connections by the local formula $A^u=u^{-1}Au+u^{-1}du$, and let $Z_N=\{\zeta I_N:\zeta^N=1\}$. Measure $C^1$ closeness by coefficient and first-derivative suprema in a fixed finite bundle atlas. For every $A\in\mathcal A_\infty^*$, a finite tuple of based piecewise-smooth loops has holonomies with no common nonzero proper invariant subspace; the same tuple continues to witness irreducibility on a $C^1$ neighborhood of $A$, so $\mathcal A_\infty^*$ is open in the $C^\infty$ topology. The stabilizer of $A$ in $\mathcal G_{q+1}$ is exactly $Z_N$. Irreducibility here does not assert $\operatorname{Hol}_A=SU(N)$.

Let $N\ge2$, $r\ge1$, and $1\le k<N$. For each orthogonal projection $P$ onto a complex $k$-plane in $\mathbb C^N$, write $V_P=\operatorname{ran}P$. Define
$$
I_{k,r}=\{(g_1,\ldots,g_r,P)\in SU(N)^r\times\operatorname{Gr}_{\mathbb C}(k,N):g_iV_P=V_P\text{ for every }i\},
$$
where $SU(N)$ has its usual matrix Lie-group structure and $\operatorname{Gr}_{\mathbb C}(k,N)$ has the orthogonal-projection topology. Then $I_{k,r}$ is a closed embedded smooth submanifold,
$$
\dim I_{k,r}=2k(N-k)+r\bigl(k^2+(N-k)^2-1\bigr).
$$
Its codimension in $SU(N)^r\times\operatorname{Gr}_{\mathbb C}(k,N)$ is $2r\,k(N-k)$, and
$$
\dim SU(N)^r-\dim I_{k,r}=2(r-1)k(N-k).
$$

Let $F(t,x,\lambda)$ be jointly $C^\infty$ in $(t,x,\lambda)$ on an open time-state-parameter
domain. Near any base data $(t_0,x_0,\lambda_0)$ there are a compact time
interval $I$ and a neighbourhood $W$ of $(x_0,\lambda_0)$ such that, for every
$(y,\lambda)\in W$, the solution of

$$x'(t)=F(t,x(t),\lambda),\qquad x(t_0)=y,$$

is defined on $I$, and the resulting solution map is smooth in the pair
$(y,\lambda)$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathcal F:M\times S\to N$ be a smooth family of maps and let $Z\subseteq N$
be an embedded submanifold. If $\mathcal F\pitchfork Z$, then the set of
parameters $s\in S$ for which the slice $\mathcal F_s:M\to N$ fails to be
transverse to $Z$ is a null subset of $S$.

Let $F:M^m\to N^n$ be smooth, let $q\in N$ be a regular value, and assume
$F^{-1}(q)$ is nonempty. Then $F^{-1}(q)$ is an embedded submanifold of
codimension $n$. Equivalently, it has dimension $m-n$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $F:M\to N$ be a smooth map between smooth manifolds. Then the critical value
set of $F$ is a null subset of $N$.

Let $M$ be a positive-dimensional smooth manifold, let $\mathcal A$ be a smooth
atlas on $M$, and let $E\subseteq M$ be $\mathcal A$-null in the sense of
[[def-null-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold]]. Then $M\setminus E$ is dense in $M$.
In particular, under Countable Choice the conclusion holds for any manifold-null
set $E$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Every subset of a manifold null set is
null, and every countable union of manifold null sets is null.

derivations.claim: If $K=\varnothing$ or $f(K)\subseteq\mathcal A_\infty^*$, the constant homotopy suffices. Otherwise realize the given finite simplicial complex by its barycentric coordinates as a compact subset of $\mathbb R^q$, taking $q\ge1$. Let $U=f^{-1}(\mathcal A_\infty^*)$, an open neighborhood of $L$ by [F2]. Choose nested relatively open neighborhoods $U_0,U_1,U_2$ of $L$ in $K$ with $\overline U_0\subset U_1$, $\overline U_1\subset U_2$, and $\overline U_2\subset U$; if $L=\varnothing$ take them empty. The compact family $f(\overline U_2)$ is uniformly stable under a sufficiently small $C^1$ perturbation: each member has the finite-loop positive margin in [F2], and a finite subcover gives one positive tolerance. Include this $C^1$ norm among the finitely many seminorms in which all forthcoming approximations are to be small.

Fix a small positive tolerance $\delta$ in each of those seminorms. Uniform continuity on compact $K$ gives a radius $\rho>0$ so that $f(s_i)-f(s)$ is smaller than $\delta$ in every selected seminorm when $s,s_i\in K$ and $|s-s_i|<2\rho$. Choose finitely many $s_i\in K$ with the balls $B_\rho(s_i)$ covering $K$. Let $\psi_i$ be nonnegative smooth ambient bumps supported in $B_{2\rho}(s_i)$ and positive on $B_\rho(s_i)$, constructed by translating and rescaling $\exp(-1/(1-|x|^2))$ on the unit ball and extending by zero. On the open neighborhood $V=\{\sum_i\psi_i>0\}$ of $K$, put $\lambda_i=\psi_i/\sum_j\psi_j$ and $g(s)=A_0+\sum_i\lambda_i(s)(f(s_i)-A_0)$. This is an ambient smooth finite-affine family of smooth connections. For $s\in K$, every contributing sample is within $2\rho$ of $s$, so $p(g(s)-f(s))<\delta$ for each selected seminorm $p$. This construction smooths the parameter dependence directly and simultaneously on the whole polyhedron; it changes no face independently of its cofaces.

Choose a smooth ambient cutoff $0\le\theta\le1$ which is zero on a neighborhood of $\overline U_0$ and one on a neighborhood of the disjoint compact set $K\setminus U_1$. Such a cutoff follows from finitely many ambient bumps separating the two compact sets. Define on $K$ the continuous family $h(s)=f(s)+\theta(s)(g(s)-f(s))$. The straight interpolation from $f$ to $h$ is fixed near $L$ and is $\delta$-small in every selected seminorm. By the uniform $C^1$ margin in step 1.1, choosing $\delta$ small ensures it is irreducible on $\overline U_2$. Its closed reducible-parameter set $R=\{s\in K:h(s)\notin\mathcal A_\infty^*\}$ is compact and contained in $K\setminus U_2$, hence in the ambient open region where $\theta=1$ and $h=g$ on $K$. If $R$ is empty the first interpolation already proves the result. Otherwise choose an ambient open $W$ with compact closure in $V\cap\{\theta=1\}$, containing $R$ and avoiding a neighborhood of $L$, and a smooth cutoff $0\le\chi\le1$ with compact support $T\subset W$, positive on $R$. All subsequent holonomy calculations use the ambient family $g$ on $W$; on the actual parameter subset $K\cap W$ this is exactly $h$.

Choose $r\ge2$ so that $2(r-1)(N-1)>q$, where $q$ is the ambient parameter dimension in step 1.1. In $M\setminus\{m\}\cong\mathbb R^d$ choose $r$ disjoint closed coordinate balls. Their exterior is path connected for $d=3$ or $4$: a polygonal path can be detoured along the connected boundary spheres of the finitely many balls, and a ray outside a large ball reaches $m$. For each ball join its boundary to $m$ through that exterior, enter the ball, run once around a small embedded circle, and return along the entering path. These are based piecewise-smooth loops $\ell_i$. Choose a closed arc on each small circle away from the entering point; it has a tube inside that ball meeting its own loop only on that arc and meeting no other loop. Thus each loop has a private control tube. The entering and returning stems are outside every private tube.

Let $U_i(s,t)$ be parallel transport for $g(s)$ from the chosen base frame to a point at parameter $t$ of $\ell_i$. It is smooth in $s\in W$ and in $t$ on each segment by [F4], applied on finitely many common intervals along the compact loop. In tube coordinates $(t,z)$ around its private arc, choose a bump $\rho_i(t)$ of integral one supported away from the arc ends, a transverse bump $c(z)$ with $c(0)=1$, and a real basis $X_a$ of $\mathfrak{su}(N)$. In a fixed smooth frame on the tube define the adjoint-valued form $b_{i,a}(s)=\rho_i(t)c(z)U_i(s,t)X_aU_i(s,t)^{-1}\,dt$, extending its coefficients constantly in the transverse coordinates before multiplying by $c$ and extending by zero outside the tube. It is a genuine smooth bundle-valued one-form depending smoothly on the ambient parameter. Along the loop its contraction is exactly the displayed transported Lie-algebra element.

For transport $U'=-B(t)U$ and a perturbation $b(t)$, differentiate the ODE to obtain $(U^{-1}\delta U)'=-U^{-1}bU$ and hence $U(1)^{-1}\delta U(1)=-\int U(t)^{-1}b(t)U(t)\,dt$. The control form in step 5.1 makes this last integral $-X_a$ for loop $i$. The other loop holonomies do not vary, since their images miss its tube. Therefore, for $D=r(N^2-1)$ parameters $w=(w_{i,a})$, the derivative at $w=0$ of $\Psi(s,w)=(\operatorname{Hol}_{\ell_i}(g(s)+\sum_{j,a}w_{j,a}b_{j,a}(s)))_{i=1}^r$ is an isomorphism in the $w$ variable onto $T SU(N)^r$, for every $s\in W$. Smooth ODE dependence and compactness of $T$ give a number $a>0$ on which this derivative remains an isomorphism uniformly for $s\in T$ and $|w|<a$.

Choose a ball $B\subset\mathbb R^D$ about zero of radius less than $a$ and put $\Phi(s,v)=\Psi(s,\chi(s)v)$ for $s\in W$. Where $\chi(s)>0$, its parameter derivative is $\chi(s)D_w\Psi(s,\chi(s)v)$, still invertible by step 6.1. For each $1\le k<N$, the map $\mathcal F_k:((W_+\times\operatorname{Gr}_{\mathbb C}(k,N))\times B)\to SU(N)^r\times\operatorname{Gr}_{\mathbb C}(k,N)$, $((s,Q),v)\mapsto(\Phi(s,v),Q)$, with $W_+=\{s\in W:\chi(s)>0\}$, is a submersion and thus transverse to $I_{k,r}$ of [F3]. Notice that the smooth source is the ambient open set $W_+$, not an individual simplex or a nonsmooth polyhedron.

By [F5], outside a null subset of $B$ the fixed-$v$ map from $W_+\times\operatorname{Gr}_{\mathbb C}(k,N)$ is transverse to $I_{k,r}$. Its source dimension is $q+2k(N-k)$, while that incidence manifold has codimension $2r k(N-k)$ by [F3]. Since $k(N-k)\ge N-1$ and $2(r-1)(N-1)>q$, the codimension is strictly larger than the source dimension. A transverse slice can therefore have no incidence preimage: a putative preimage would require a surjection from a smaller-dimensional tangent space to the normal space.

Equivalently, [F7] applied in local incidence charts makes $Z_k=\mathcal F_k^{-1}(I_{k,r})$ a smooth manifold of dimension $q+D-2(r-1)k(N-k)<D$. Every point of its projection to $B$ is critical, so [F8] makes its image null. There are finitely many $k$, and [F9] makes the union of these images and the exceptional sets in step 8.1 null with dense complement. Thus arbitrarily small $v\in B$ avoid every incidence condition throughout $W_+$. This also directly verifies the transversality dimension argument by Sard.

Define on all of $K$ the final family $h_v(s)=h(s)+\chi(s)\sum_{j,a}v_{j,a}b_{j,a}(s)$, with the added term zero off $W$. The compact support $T$ and its spatial smoothness make this term continuous in every section seminorm, and its value uniformly small in any specified finite list by taking $v$ sufficiently small. If $\chi(s)>0$, then $s\in W$ and $h(s)=g(s)$, so $h_v(s)$ has the holonomy tuple $\Phi(s,v)$, which has no common invariant proper subspace by step 9.1. Therefore $h_v(s)$ is irreducible. If $\chi(s)=0$, then $s\notin R$ since $\chi$ is positive on $R$, so $h_v(s)=h(s)$ was already irreducible. The straight perturbation homotopy from $h$ to $h_v$ is fixed on an open neighborhood of $L$. Concatenate it with the interpolation in step 3.1. Choose $\delta$ and then $v$ within half of each requested seminorm tolerance; the triangle inequality gives the asserted bounds relative to the original $f$ for the entire concatenated homotopy. All formulas are global on $K$, so faces and cofaces agree automatically.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Let $\mathcal A_\infty:=A_0+\Omega^1(M,\operatorname{ad}P)$ and let $\mathcal G_\infty$ be the smooth gauge group, with the $C^\infty$ section topology generated by all finite-atlas derivative seminorms. Define $\bar{\mathcal G}_\infty:=\mathcal G_\infty/Z_N$. In a local section of $P$, write a connection as a matrix-valued one-form $A$ and a gauge section as a map $u$ into $SU(N)$; the right gauge action is $A^u:=u^{-1}Au+u^{-1}du$, equivalently pullback by the gauge automorphism associated with $u$. The calculus lemma proves that this formula defines a smooth action on the Sobolev spaces above. For an adjoint section $\xi$, set $d_A\xi:=d\xi+[A,\xi]$ using the degree-one Lie-algebra-valued-form bracket. In local coordinates and an orthonormal adjoint frame, define the formal adjoint on an adjoint-valued one-form $a$ by $(d_A^*a)=-g^{ij}(\nabla_i^{\mathrm{LC}}a_j+[A_i,a_j])$, where $\nabla^{\mathrm{LC}}$ differentiates the covector index. This is the $L^2$ adjoint for the Riemannian volume and stated fiber metric; its local coefficient formula defines a distribution at Sobolev regularity.

Assume ZF together with the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be $S^3$ or $S^4$ with its compact, connected, oriented, boundaryless smooth structure, let $N\ge2$, and let $P\to M$ be a smooth principal right $SU(N)$-bundle with a smooth reference connection $A_0$. Fix a basepoint $m\in M$ and a frame of $P_m$. Equip $\mathcal A_\infty=A_0+\Omega^1(M;\operatorname{ad}P)$ with the Fréchet topology generated by suprema of all derivatives of section coefficients in a fixed finite bundle atlas. Let $\mathcal A_\infty^*$ consist of connections whose based holonomy action on $\mathbb C^N$ has no nonzero proper invariant complex subspace. Let $K$ be the geometric realization of a finite simplicial complex, let $L$ be the realization of a subcomplex, and let $f:K\to\mathcal A_\infty$ be continuous with $f(L)\subseteq\mathcal A_\infty^*$. Then there is a continuous homotopy $H:K\times[0,1]\to\mathcal A_\infty$, fixed on $L$ and on an open neighborhood of $L$, such that $H(\cdot,1)$ maps all of $K$ into $\mathcal A_\infty^*$. For every finite list of these $C^\infty$ section seminorms $p_1,\ldots,p_m$ and positive tolerances $\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_m$, the homotopy can be chosen with $\sup_{(s,t)\in K\times[0,1]}p_j(H(s,t)-f(s))<\epsilon_j$ for every $j$.

Let $I=[0,1]$, $n\ge1$, and $x_0\in X$. Write $\partial I^n$ for the points with at least one coordinate 0 or 1. The set $\pi_n(X,x_0)$ consists of continuous $a:I^n\to X$ with $a(\partial I^n)=\{x_0\}$, modulo homotopies fixed on that entire boundary. This is a quotient by an equivalence relation by [[cor-homotopy-relative-and-path-homotopy-are-equivalence-relations]].

derivations.claim: The affine space $\mathcal A_\infty$ contains $A_0$. Apply [F2] to the constant map from a one-point polyhedron with empty subpolyhedron and value $A_0$. Its endpoint is an element of $\mathcal A_\infty^*$, proving nonemptiness.

Let $A,B\in\mathcal A_\infty^*$. The affine path $\gamma(t)=(1-t)A+tB$ is continuous in the Fréchet topology and has irreducible endpoints. Apply [F2] with $K=I$ and $L=\{0,1\}$. The resulting endpoint path remains in $\mathcal A_\infty^*$ and fixes both endpoints, so the locus is path-connected.

Fix $j\ge1$ and a based representative $u:(I^j,\partial I^j)\to(\mathcal A_\infty^*,A)$. The quotient $I^j/\partial I^j$ is homeomorphic to $S^j$, so regard $u$ as a continuous sphere map with value $A$ at the collapsed boundary point. Identify $D^{j+1}$ with the cone on $S^j$ and define $F([r,x])=A_0+r(u(x)-A_0)$ for $0\le r\le1$. For each continuous section seminorm $p$, compactness of $S^j$ gives $C_p=\sup_x p(u(x)-A_0)<\infty$; hence $p(F([r,x])-A_0)\le rC_p\to0$ as $r\to0$. This proves continuity at the cone apex in every defining seminorm, and away from the apex continuity follows from continuity of $u$ and affine operations. Thus $F:D^{j+1}\to\mathcal A_\infty$ is a continuous filling of $u$.

Apply [F2] to $F$ with $K=D^{j+1}$ and $L=\partial D^{j+1}=S^j$. Its boundary is already irreducible, so the endpoint is a map $G:D^{j+1}\to\mathcal A_\infty^*$ agreeing with $u$ on the boundary. Choose the based point $x_0\in S^j$ with $u(x_0)=A$. Since the disk is convex, $C_t(x)=(1-t)x+tx_0$ remains in the disk and fixes $x_0$. Then $G(C_t(x))$ is a homotopy from $G$ to the constant map at $A$ that fixes $x_0$ and remains in $\mathcal A_\infty^*$. Restricting it to $S^j$ gives a based nullhomotopy of $u$; by [F3], its class in $\pi_j(\mathcal A_\infty^*,A)$ is zero. Since $j$ and $u$ were arbitrary, every stated homotopy group vanishes.

Assume ZF together with the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be $S^3$ or $S^4$, let $N\ge2$, and let $P\to M$ be any smooth principal right $SU(N)$-bundle. Fix a smooth reference connection $A_0$, a basepoint $m\in M$, and a frame of $P_m$. Equip the affine space $\mathcal A_\infty=A_0+\Omega^1(M;\operatorname{ad}P)$ with its $C^\infty$ section topology, and let $\mathcal A_\infty^*$ be the connections whose based holonomy action on $\mathbb C^N$ has no nonzero proper invariant complex subspace. Then $\mathcal A_\infty^*$ is nonempty and path-connected, and for every $A\in\mathcal A_\infty^*$ and every integer $j\ge1$, $\pi_j(\mathcal A_\infty^*,A)=0$. Here $\pi_j(X,x)$ is the based homotopy group of continuous maps $u:(I^j,\partial I^j)\to(X,x)$ modulo homotopies that keep $\partial I^j$ at $x$.

derivations.claim: The zero connection has parallel transport equal to the identity in the product trivialization, so its based holonomy group is $\{I_N\}$. Since $N\ge2$, every complex line in $\mathbb C^N$ is a nonzero proper subspace invariant under $I_N$. Thus $0\notin\mathcal A_\infty^*$.

The cone $D^{j+1}=CS^j$ identifies all $(0,x)$ to one apex and has boundary parameter $r=1$. The formula $F([r,x])=r f(x)$ is well-defined because it is independent of $x$ at $r=0$, and equals $f(x)$ at $r=1$. For every continuous section seminorm $p$, compactness of $S^j$ gives $C_p=\sup_x p(f(x))<\infty$, so $p(F([r,x]))\le rC_p\to0$ as $r\to0$. Away from the apex, continuity follows from continuity of $f$ and scalar multiplication in the Fréchet vector space. Hence $F$ is a continuous affine filling in $\mathcal A_\infty$.

By step 1.1, the apex value lies outside $\mathcal A_\infty^*$; therefore this explicit extension is not an irreducible filling, regardless of its irreducible boundary values. In particular, convexity of the full affine space does not imply convexity of its irreducible subset.

Apply [F2] to $F$ with $K=D^{j+1}$ and $L=S^j$. The lemma fixes the boundary and supplies a homotopic endpoint $\widetilde F:D^{j+1}\to\mathcal A_\infty^*$. If $x_0\in S^j$ is the based point with $f(x_0)=A$, the maps $x\mapsto\widetilde F((1-t)x+tx_0)$ stay in the disk, remain in $\mathcal A_\infty^*$, and fix $x_0$. Their restriction to the boundary is a based nullhomotopy of $f$.

Theorem [F3] supplies such irreducible sphere families, for example the constant family at any irreducible connection, and identifies the conclusion with vanishing of $\pi_j(\mathcal A_\infty^*,A)$. The example therefore isolates the precise role of relative avoidance: it upgrades a continuous affine filling, which may hit a reducible connection, to an irreducible filling without moving the sphere family.
